title: Two Study 2 index effects and the one-sided test
location: p. 43, with the test on p. 39
published: Figure 7 shows that in Study 2, the effects on these post-treatment outcomes were also null
note: Recorded as a note, for the authors to rule on. Page 39 sets a one-sided cutoff of 0.025 in the pro-Democratic direction. The deposit's script applies the lower tail to every Pro-Democratic row, which is that direction for party ID (1 = Strong Democrat) and the opposite one for the two 0-1 indexes, where higher is more Democratic. Its Study 2 one-sided p-values on those indexes read 0.981 and 0.989. In the stated direction they are 0.0188 (evaluation, 0.010, SE 0.005) and 0.0109 (identification, 0.010, SE 0.004), both below the cutoff. Neither survives correction across the 96 tests (Benjamini-Hochberg 0.435), and the estimates are about 0.01 on a 0-1 scale. Party ID stays null. Figure 7's numbers are unchanged. Separately, the Study 1 script matches a label it has already renamed, so all 24 of its Pro-Democratic one-sided p-values are missing. With that repaired, the same page's "one significant result" among subgroups still holds, at 0.009.

title: Near 100% power
published: this, despite achieving near 100% power for the estimated effect sizes from Study 1
note: Recorded as a note, for the authors to rule on. The pre-analysis plan's near-100% figure is a design-stage simulation under its own outcome model, which I did not rerun. Study 2's realized standard errors on party ID are 0.024 and 0.023, which give about 0.53 and 0.59 power against 0.05 at the two-sided 0.05 level, the same as a one-sided 0.025 test up to a negligible tail. Page 33's "to ensure near 100% power" describes the design and is not in question.
